# Build notes — issue #1944: run-level wall-clock limit with watchdog

## What I've read
- All 4 test files (SPEC 1-4)
- run-open-items-test.sh (O9: expects exactly 6 `error` lines in runner.sh matching pattern)
- runner-pipeline-end-test.sh (T9: iterates STATUSES array for golden files)
- scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — where to add _runner_resolve_run_limit_s
- core/pipeline/template.sh — where to add template_max_run_s()
- core/pipeline/runner.sh — traps, _runner_end_on_abort, glyph/color functions
- scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh — word list comment, arm sentinel
- scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh — run_end_words (need timed_out case)
- core/state/resume.sh — get_resume_recommendation (need timed_out case)
- docs/adr/ADR-025-abort-propagation.md — Enforced by section
- docs/adr/ADR-054-stage-contract.md — need §11
- config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt — need to remove ADR-054

## Implementation plan
1. stage-limits.sh: add _runner_resolve_run_limit_s()
2. template.sh: add template_max_run_s() (reads top-level max_run_s: key)
3. abort-propagation.sh: add timed_out to word list comment
4. run-open-items.sh: add timed_out case to run_end_words()
5. resume.sh: add timed_out case to get_resume_recommendation()
6. runner.sh:
   - Source stage-limits.sh in preamble
   - Add _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S and _RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID globals
   - Add timed_out to _pipeline_status_glyph/_pipeline_status_color
   - Add timed_out to _runner_render_open_items
   - Add timed_out case to _runner_end_on_abort (error message with run_end_words)
   - In main(): call _runner_resolve_run_limit_s after load_template; exit misconfigured if fails
   - In _runner_signal_trap: after arming, read back abort reason (so timed_out wins)
   - In _runner_abort_trap: check for timed_out, use different status path
   - Kill watchdog in EXIT trap before dispatch_always_run
   - Arm watchdog after traps installed and resume sentinel disarmed
7. ADR-025: add timed_out to word list, extend ## Enforced by
8. ADR-054: add §11, add ## Enforced by
9. config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt: remove ADR-054-stage-contract.md
10. runner-pipeline-end-test.sh: add timed_out to STATUSES array
11. Create golden files for timed_out
12. ADR-006: add timed_out to pipeline status enum table
13. ADR-015: add timed_out row to glyph/color table

## Key decisions
- Watchdog: background subshell that sleeps, arms sentinel, then sends TERM to PG via raw kill
  (NOT zbuild_pg_kill — the design says watchdog is IN the runner's PG)
- In _runner_signal_trap: change `_RUNNER_ABORT_REASON="$_word"` to 
  `_RUNNER_ABORT_REASON="$(_zbuild_abort_reason)"` so timed_out wins over sigterm
- In _runner_abort_trap: add check for timed_out abort reason before the "interrupted" path
- Misconfigured path: resolve limit after load_template, before init_state; print to stderr

## Status
- [ ] stage-limits.sh
- [ ] template.sh
- [ ] abort-propagation.sh
- [ ] run-open-items.sh
- [ ] resume.sh
- [ ] runner.sh
- [ ] ADR-025
- [ ] ADR-054
- [ ] adr-enforcement-baseline.txt
- [ ] runner-pipeline-end-test.sh
- [ ] golden files
- [ ] ADR-006, ADR-015

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/unit/run-limit-precedence-test.sh — run-level wall-clock limit (#1944)
#
# SPEC-2 [code]:
#   _runner_resolve_run_limit_s resolves template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S >
#   20700; a non-integer or non-positive value in template or env yields
#   disposition misconfigured and the run does not reach the dispatch loop.
#
# SPEC-5 [no-code]:
#   The limit is resolved from template, env, or constant only; scripts/lib/
#   stage-limits.sh and core/pipeline/runner.sh contain no reference to
#   GITHUB_ACTIONS, CI, or any platform-specific variable in the new code.
#
# SPEC-6 [no-code]:
#   ADR-025 names timed_out in its word vocabulary with ## Enforced by entries
#   citing the new tests; ADR-054 gains a §11 for the run-level limit with
#   ## Enforced by; config/adr-enforcement-baseline.txt no longer lists
#   ADR-054-stage-contract.md.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-limit-precedence: max_run_s resolution + platform-free + ADR alignment (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-limit-precedence"

RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
STAGE_LIMITS="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"

# ─── SPEC-2: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s ────────────────────────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh
source "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined in stage-limits.sh" \
        "function not found after sourcing scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence: template max_run_s > ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S > 20700"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Case 1: no template value, no env → falls back to default 20700
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] no template, no env → default 20700" "20700" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"

    # Case 2: env only → uses env
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] env ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600 used when no template value" "3600" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 3: template value > env → template wins
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '7200'; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=3600
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S" "7200" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Case 4: template value only (no env) → template wins over default
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '1800'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || true
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value wins over default" "1800" "${_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S:-}"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] precedence checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer / non-positive → misconfigured, rc=1"

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # Non-integer in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf 'not-a-number'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-positive (zero) in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf '0'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] template value=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Negative in template
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf -- '-5'; }
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] negative template value → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"

    # Non-integer in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="thirty"
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] non-integer ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S

    # Non-positive in ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
    _RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
    template_max_run_s() { printf ''; }
    ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0
    _rc2=0
    _runner_resolve_run_limit_s 2>/dev/null || _rc2=$?
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=0 → rc=1" "1" "$_rc2"
    unset ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] validation checks skipped — function not found" "missing implementation"
fi

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-2] misconfigured run: runner rejects invalid limit before dispatch"
# Run the actual runner with an invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S; it must exit non-zero
# before dispatching any stage (no stage marker written).
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state-miscfg"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events-miscfg"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1

# Minimal single-stage plugin
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

MISCFG_OVERLAY="$(setup_git_temp_repo miscfg-run-limit)"

cat > "$MISCFG_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates/limit-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: limit-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50

STAGE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/stage-ran-marker"
cat > "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/agent/intake/plugin.sh" <<PLUG

    : > "${STAGE_MARKER}"
    $(mock_v2_result_line intake)
    return 0
}
PLUG

set +e
ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="not-a-number" \
( cd "$MISCFG_OVERLAY" && bash "$RUNNER" --template limit-single --goal "test misconfigured limit" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stderr"
_miscfg_rc=$?
set -e

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] invalid ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S → runner exits non-zero" "1" "$_miscfg_rc"
if [[ -e "$STAGE_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when limit is misconfigured" \
        "stage marker exists — dispatch loop was reached"
else
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] stage did not run when limit is misconfigured"
fi

# Check pipeline-state.json reflects misconfigured disposition
_miscfg_sf="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
if [[ -f "$_miscfg_sf" ]]; then
    _miscfg_disp="$(jq -r '.disposition // empty' "$_miscfg_sf" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-2] pipeline-state.json disposition=misconfigured" "misconfigured" "$_miscfg_disp"
else
    # State file may be absent if the runner refuses before creating it; check stderr instead
    if grep -qi "misconfigured\|invalid.*max_run_s\|max_run_s.*invalid\|non-integer\|non-positive\|max_run_s.*must be" \
            "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stderr" 2>/dev/null; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-2] stderr explains misconfigured limit"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-2] runner names misconfigured limit on stderr" \
            "stderr: $(head -c 400 "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/miscfg.stderr" 2>/dev/null)"
    fi
fi

# ─── SPEC-5: no platform-specific env vars in new limit code ────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-5] stage-limits.sh contains no GITHUB_ACTIONS or bare CI reference"

# GITHUB_ACTIONS check — never acceptable in limit resolution
_ga_count_sl="$(grep -c 'GITHUB_ACTIONS' "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true)"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] stage-limits.sh: no GITHUB_ACTIONS reference" "0" "$_ga_count_sl"

# $CI or ${CI} in non-comment code lines in stage-limits.sh
_ci_sl="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '\$\{?CI\}?[^A-Za-z0-9_]' || true)"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] stage-limits.sh: no bare \$CI in non-comment code" "0" "$_ci_sl"

# runner.sh: no GITHUB_ACTIONS in code lines (excluding pure comments)
_ga_rn="$(grep -v '^[[:space:]]*#' "$RUNNER" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'GITHUB_ACTIONS' || true)"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-5] runner.sh: no GITHUB_ACTIONS in code lines" "0" "$_ga_rn"

# ─── SPEC-6: ADR alignment ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 names timed_out in its word vocabulary"
ADR025="$REPO_ROOT/docs/adr/ADR-025-abort-propagation.md"

if [[ ! -f "$ADR025" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-6] ADR-025 file exists" "not found: $ADR025"
else
    # The word vocabulary line lists the abort words; timed_out must be among them
    _vocab_line="$(grep -E '(sigint|sigterm|cycle_abort).*timed_out|timed_out.*(sigint|sigterm|cycle_abort)' \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh — the limits a stage's model calls run under.
#
# One copy, two readers: the router enforces these numbers on every call
# (core/router/route.sh) and the engine states them to the stage in its rules
# (scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh, ADR-067 §8). A stage told a different budget
# from the one it is killed at works until it is killed.
#
# Sourced library: inherits the caller's shell options; do NOT add set -euo.
[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_STAGE_LIMITS_LOADED=1

if ! declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # shellcheck source=../../core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh
    source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/core/plugin-registry/manifest-router-budget.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# ─── _route_manifest_knob <knob> — ADR-017 §11 (#1816) manifest layer ───────
# The dispatched plugin's OWN declared default, read from its manifest via the
# dispatch identity the engine exports at plugin_hook_call (ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR,
# ADR-054 §3 / #1862). Empty whenever there is no dispatch, no manifest, no
# declaration — or a declaration this router cannot use.
#
# Out-of-range and non-numeric values are IGNORED here, not fatal: the loud
# gate is validate_manifest at load, and a plugin that got past it with a bad
# value must fall back to the constant rather than hand the router a 0-second
# timeout. Fail-safe on the hot path, fail-loud at the boundary.
_route_manifest_knob() {
    local knob="$1"
    local dir="${ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$dir" && -f "$dir/manifest.yaml" ]] || return 0
    declare -F manifest_router_knob >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    local v; v="$(manifest_router_knob "$dir/manifest.yaml" "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local range; range="$(_manifest_router_range "$knob" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$range" ]] || return 0
    local min="${range% *}" max="${range#* }"
    [[ "$v" -ge "$min" && "$v" -le "$max" ]] || return 0
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

# ─── _route_resolve_knob — ADR-017 (#455) precedence chokepoint ──────────────
# Generic helper: future knobs (tier_default, budget_usd, model_override) reuse
# this. Accessor returns per-stage value or empty; env_var supplies session-wide
# fallback; manifest_knob (#1816) names the plugin's own declared default; the
# compile-time constant is the floor:
#
#   template accessor  >  env var  >  manifest config.router.*  >  constant
#
# The manifest sits BELOW env and template because it is a default, not an
# override: a flow may right-size a stage for a fast lane, and the operator
# escape hatch must still beat both. It sits ABOVE the constant because that is
# what the constant always was — a default nobody could state per stage.
_route_resolve_knob() {
    local accessor_fn="$1" env_var="$2" default_val="$3"
    local override_event="${4:-router.timeout.override_ignored}"
    local manifest_knob="${5:-}"
    local v=""
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F "$accessor_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        v="$($accessor_fn "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    if [[ -n "$v" ]]; then
        # If env var ALSO set and differs, emit override-ignored event for audit.
        # A manifest value losing to template or env is NOT this case: a default
        # being replaced is the design, and eventing it would make every
        # declaring plugin noisy on every dispatch.
        local env_val="${!env_var:-}"
        if [[ -n "$env_val" && "$env_val" != "$v" ]]; then
            eb_emit_event "$override_event" \
                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" \
                "env_var=$env_var" \
                "env_value=$env_val" \
                "applied=$v" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        printf '%s\n' "$v"; return 0
    fi
    local env_v="${!env_var:-}"
    if [[ -n "$env_v" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "$env_v"; return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "$manifest_knob" ]]; then
        local mv; mv="$(_route_manifest_knob "$manifest_knob")"
        if [[ -n "$mv" ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "$mv"; return 0
        fi
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$default_val"
}

# Concrete: per-stage router.timeout_s > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT >
# manifest config.router.timeout_s > 300s default.
_route_resolve_timeout() {
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_timeout ZBUILD_ROUTER_TIMEOUT 300 \
        router.timeout.override_ignored timeout_s
}

# ADR-018 (#466): per-stage router.max_turns > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS > 25 default.
# ADR-029 G3 (#812): when the cycle orchestrator detects a router timeout for
# this stage, it sets ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE so the next dispatch
# of the same stage uses an escalated budget (+50%, capped at 2× base). The
# override wins over the per-stage template AND the env knob because that's
# the entire point — escalation must beat the static config that already
# proved too small.
_route_resolve_max_turns() {
    if [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS_OVERRIDE"
        return 0
    fi
    _route_resolve_knob template_stage_router_max_turns ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS 25 \
        router.max_turns.override_ignored max_turns
}

# ADR-018 Amendment N (#762): when max_turns resolves to the 0 sentinel,
# classify which source set it (template > env > manifest > default) for
# telemetry. Emits `template`, `env`, `manifest` (#1816), or `default`. The
# `default` branch is currently unreachable (compile-time default is 25, not 0)
# but kept for forward compatibility if the default ever changes.
# Copilot review #764: compare numerically so "00", "000" etc. (accepted
# by the ^[0-9]+$ validator) classify correctly.
_route_classify_max_turns_source() {
    local _tpl_val=""
    if [[ -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] \
        && command -v template_stage_router_max_turns >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _tpl_val="$(template_stage_router_max_turns "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    local _mf_val; _mf_val="$(_route_manifest_knob max_turns)"
    if [[ "$_tpl_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_tpl_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "template"
    elif [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS:-}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "${ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_TURNS}" -eq 0 ]]; then
        printf '%s' "env"
    elif [[ "$_mf_val" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [[ "$_mf_val" -eq 0 ]]; then
        # #1816: a plugin that declares `max_turns: 0` owns that sentinel. Left
        # unclassified it would be recorded as `default`, which is the one thing
        # it is not — the record would name a source that declared nothing.
        printf '%s' "manifest"
    else
        printf '%s' "default"
    fi
}

# ADR-018 (#467): per-stage router.max_iterations > $ZBUILD_ROUTER_MAX_ITERATIONS > 10 default.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tests/unit/run-watchdog-clean-exit-test.sh — clean-exit watchdog lifecycle (#1944)
#
# SPEC-3 [code]:
#   A run that finishes within max_run_s exits with its own pipeline status
#   unchanged; the watchdog process does not exist after the runner process exits.
#
# A test that only checks "runner exits 0" passes BEFORE implementation too.
# We discriminate by also asserting:
#   1. _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined (fails before implementation)
#   2. With ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S set, the completed run's status is the stage-reported
#      status — not timed_out (impl must not fire the watchdog on a clean run)
#   3. No pipeline.end status=timed_out in the events log (watchdog was reaped)
#   4. ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S is validated by the new function: a valid value leads to a
#      clean run; the function is the one that resolves it (not the runner ignoring it)
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-watchdog-clean-exit: watchdog reaped, status unchanged (#1944 SPEC-3)"
setup_test_env "run-watchdog-clean-exit"

RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"
STAGE_LIMITS="$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"

# ─── S3-1: _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined ───────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-3] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s defined in stage-limits.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh
source "$STAGE_LIMITS" 2>/dev/null || true

if declare -F _runner_resolve_run_limit_s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-3] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-3] _runner_resolve_run_limit_s is defined" \
        "function not found; watchdog arms only when this function exists"
fi

# ─── S3-2: clean run with max_run_s set → status unchanged, not timed_out ──
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-3] clean run with max_run_s=30 exits with complete status"

export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

# Minimal 1-stage pipeline that completes quickly (no sleep)
mock_plugin_factory "intake" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

CLEAN_OVERLAY="$(setup_git_temp_repo watchdog-clean-exit)"
mkdir -p "$CLEAN_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates"
cat > "$CLEAN_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates/watchdog-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: watchdog-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
EOF

# max_run_s=30 is generous: the pipeline completes in < 5s, well before the limit
set +e
( cd "$CLEAN_OVERLAY" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=30 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template watchdog-single --goal "clean run watchdog test" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/clean.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/clean.stderr"
_clean_rc=$?
set -e

_clean_sf="$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-3] clean run exits 0" "0" "$_clean_rc"

if [[ -f "$_clean_sf" ]]; then
    _clean_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$_clean_sf" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    # Status must be the stage-driven completion, not timed_out
    if [[ "$_clean_status" == "complete" || "$_clean_status" == "success" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-3] pipeline status is complete (not timed_out)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-3] pipeline status is complete (not timed_out)" \
            "actual status: ${_clean_status:-<empty>}"
    fi
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-3] pipeline status is NOT timed_out" "" \
        "$([[ "$_clean_status" == "timed_out" ]] && echo "timed_out" || echo "")"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-3] pipeline-state.json written" \
        "state file not found: $_clean_sf"
fi

# ─── S3-3: no timed_out event after clean run ───────────────────────────────
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-3] no pipeline.end status=timed_out in events log after clean run"

if [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _timed_out_events="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .type' \
        "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-3] no pipeline.end/timed_out event after clean run" "0" "$_timed_out_events"
else
    # Events file absent means no events fired — acceptable for a clean run
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-3] no timed_out event (events file absent)"
fi

# ─── S3-4: watchdog process reaped — no lingering sleep from the run ────────
# We cannot easily inspect the runner's internal _RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID from
# outside. We infer reaping by running with a VERY short max_run_s (3s) on a
# pipeline that completes in < 2s, then sleeping past max_run_s and confirming
# the pipeline status remains complete (not timed_out). If the watchdog were
# not reaped, it would fire at max_run_s and attempt to signal whatever is
# running — but since the runner has exited by then, the signal is benign
# (no runner to receive it). We verify the status file is not mutated.
print_test_section "[#1944/SPEC-3] watchdog reaped: status unchanged after waiting past max_run_s"

rm -f "$ZBUILD_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json" "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL"

set +e
( cd "$CLEAN_OVERLAY" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=5 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template watchdog-single --goal "watchdog reaped test" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/reaped.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/reaped.stderr"
_reaped_rc=$?
set -e

# Status captured immediately after runner exits
_status_before_wait=""
if [[ -f "$_clean_sf" ]]; then
    _status_before_wait="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$_clean_sf" 2>/dev/null || true)"
fi

# Wait past max_run_s=5 by 2 seconds: if watchdog is not reaped, it fires here
sleep 7

# Status must not have changed — a live orphan watchdog cannot mutate the state
# file (the runner process that writes the file has already exited), but we
# verify no NEW timed_out event appeared in the log since the runner exited.
_timed_out_after_wait=0
if [[ -f "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _timed_out_after_wait="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .type' \
        "$ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ' || echo 0)"
fi

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-3] runner exits 0 with max_run_s=5 on a quick stage" "0" "$_reaped_rc"
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-3] no timed_out event after waiting past max_run_s" "0" "$_timed_out_after_wait"

cleanup_test_env
print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

mock_plugin_factory() {
    local id="$1" kind="${2:-agent}" exit_code="${3:-0}" platform="${4:-}" role="${5:-}" version="${6:-0.0.1}"
    local dir="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins/$kind/$id"
    mkdir -p "$dir"
    fixture_link_personas "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
    local fn; fn="${id//-/_}_run"
    cat > "$dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
id: $id
name: Test $id
kind: $kind
version: $version
hooks:
  run: $fn
requires:
  core:
    - redaction
EOF
    [[ -n "$platform" ]] && printf 'platform: %s\n' "$platform" >> "$dir/manifest.yaml"
    printf 'provides:\n  result_contract: 2\n' >> "$dir/manifest.yaml"
    [[ -n "$role" ]] && printf '  role: %s\n' "$role" >> "$dir/manifest.yaml"
    cat >> "$dir/manifest.yaml" <<EOF
outputs:
  - id: ${id//-/_}_result
    path: \${artifact_dir}/${id}-result.json
    type: ${id}-result.json@1
    format: json
    required: true
    primary: true
config:
  valid_verdicts: [pass, error]
EOF
    local _verdict=pass _disp=complete
    [[ "$exit_code" -ne 0 ]] && { _verdict=error; _disp=broken; }
    cat > "$dir/plugin.sh" <<EOF
${fn}() {
    local _art; _art="\${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-\$(dirname "\$2")/artifacts}"
    mkdir -p "\$_art"
    printf '{"result_contract":2,"verdict":"%s","disposition":"%s","reason":"mock %s"}' \\
        "$_verdict" "$_disp" "$id" > "\$_art/${id}-result.json"
    return $exit_code
}
EOF
    printf '%s\n' "$dir"
}

# ── zb_engine_loop_state ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Writes one loop's record into a pipeline-state.json with the ENGINE's own
# writers (_cycle_state_init / _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic,
# core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh): <rounds> rounds, then <final status>.
# #1799: a hand-written `cycle_iterations` holds whatever its author assumed —
# a field the engine never writes passed a test that wrote it itself.
# scripts/lib/lint-test-engine-state.sh refuses a hand-written one.
#
# Usage: zb_engine_loop_state <state_file> <loop id> <rounds> <limit> <final status>
zb_engine_loop_state() {
    local sf="$1" id="$2" rounds="$3" limit="$4" final="$5" root
    root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
    ( source "$root/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1
      _cycle_state_init "$sf" "$id" "$(dirname "$sf")/$id-history.jsonl" "$limit" || exit 1
      local n
      for (( n = 1; n <= rounds; n++ )); do
          _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic "$sf" "$id" "$n" fail failed 1 in_progress || exit 1
      done
      _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic "$sf" "$id" "$rounds" fail failed 1 "$final" )
}

# ── mock_v2_result_line ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# the unquoted heredoc, or the stage exits 0 with no readable result — which
# #1850 makes a failure.
#
# Usage: mock_v2_result_line <id> [verdict=pass] [disposition=complete]
mock_v2_result_line() {
    local id="$1" verdict="${2:-pass}" disp="${3:-complete}"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2016  # the $-expressions are for the stub, not here
    printf '%s' 'local _art; _art="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$(dirname "$2")/artifacts}"; mkdir -p "$_art"; '
    printf "printf '%%s' '{\"result_contract\":2,\"verdict\":\"%s\",\"disposition\":\"%s\",\"reason\":\"mock %s\"}' > \"\$_art/%s-result.json\"" \
        "$verdict" "$disp" "$id" "$id"

The test creates a template at `$CLEAN_OVERLAY/.zbuild/templates/watchdog-single.yaml` which `extends: simple`. This would need to find `simple.yaml` somewhere, which is in `config/templates/simple.yaml` in the repo root.

But the simple.yaml has a full pipeline with many stages (intake, plan, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses, review-aggregator, pr). The watchdog-single.yaml overrides with just one stage (intake). So when the runner tries to run this, it would try to validate all stages against plugins, which might fail.
Looking closer, the child template only defines the intake stage with gate set to auto and specific io settings for file destinations and tail lines. I'm wondering whether zBuild's inheritance model has the child's `stages:` replace the parent's entirely, or merge with it, since that determines whether this test actually runs just intake or the whole pipeline.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Integration: run-level wall-clock limit with watchdog (#1944)
#
# SPEC-1 [code]: a run whose wall-clock time exceeds max_run_s ends with
#   pipeline status timed_out in pipeline-state.json and pipeline.end event
#   carrying status=timed_out, the in-flight stage, and limit_s; the watchdog
#   fires even when the engine is idle between dispatches (not only inside a
#   stage); a process that ignores TERM is dead within TERM + 10 s; release and
#   persist execute on every timed-out exit path.
#
# Phases:
#   P1 — basic timeout: slow stage hits the watchdog; status=timed_out, event
#        fields correct; runner exits non-zero within the limit
#   P2 — idle between dispatches: two stages both finishing quickly; total
#        wall-clock exceeds max_run_s (via overhead or runner startup); status=timed_out
#   P3 — TERM-ignore: a stage that traps and ignores SIGTERM is dead within
#        TERM + 10 s (KILL escalation)
#   P4 — release runs: always_run release stage executes on timed-out exit path
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
RUNNER="$REPO_ROOT/core/pipeline/runner.sh"

# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh
source "$REPO_ROOT/scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh"

print_test_header "run-timed-out: wall-clock limit watchdog fires and ends run correctly (#1944)"
setup_test_env "run-timed-out"
export ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn

PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/state"
EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/events"
EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
export ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT="$PLUGINS_ROOT"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$EVENTS_DIR"
export ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$EVENTS_JSONL"
export ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json"
export ZBUILD_MODELS_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/config/models.json"
export ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=0
export ZBUILD_SCOPE_OVERRIDE=1
mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$EVENTS_DIR" "$HOME/.zbuild"
printf '%s' "bootstrap" > "$HOME/.zbuild/scope-override-token"

# ── Shared overlay repo ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OVERLAY_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo run-timed-out-overlay)"
mkdir -p "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates"

# Single-stage template: one slow stage (the main timeout victim)
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-single.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-single
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: slow-stage
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
    router:
      timeout_s: 120
      max_turns: 0
EOF

# Two-stage template: both stages return quickly; for idle-between-dispatches test
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-two-stage.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-two-stage
extends: simple
stages:
  - id: fast-one
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
  - id: fast-two
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file]
      tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Always-run (release) template: flow stage + always_run release stage
cat > "$OVERLAY_REPO/.zbuild/templates/timeout-with-release.yaml" <<'EOF'
id: timeout-with-release
extends: simple
flow:
  - outcome

always_run:
  - release

outcome:
  gate: auto
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50

release:
  gate: auto
  roles: [teardown]
  router:
    timeout_s: 30
  io:
    destinations: [file]
    tail_lines: 50
EOF

# Commit the templates into the overlay repo so the runner can find them
(cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && git add .zbuild && git commit -q -m "add timeout test templates") >/dev/null 2>&1

# ── P1: basic timeout — slow stage, status=timed_out ───────────────────────

# Stage that sleeps far longer than max_run_s
mock_plugin_factory "slow-stage" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
SLOW_STAGE_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/slow-stage-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    sleep 120
    $(mock_v2_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$STATE_DIR"
print_test_section "P1: slow stage timeout — status=timed_out written to pipeline-state.json"

# Run with ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 (2 seconds); wrap in timeout 25s to prevent hanging
# before implementation (no watchdog → stage sleeps forever → outer timeout kills it)
set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p1" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1.stderr"
p1_rc=$?
set -e

STATE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"

# Runner must exit non-zero (timed-out runs are failures)
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p1_rc"

# pipeline-state.json must exist and have status=timed_out
if [[ ! -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
else
    _p1_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline-state.json status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p1_status"
fi

print_test_section "P1: pipeline.end event fields — status=timed_out, stage, limit_s"

if [[ ! -f "$EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: events.jsonl written" "events file not found"
else
    # Event: pipeline.end with status=timed_out
    _p1_end_event="$(jq -c 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out")' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_end_event" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end status=timed_out event emitted" \
            "no such event in $(wc -l < "$EVENTS_JSONL") events"
    fi

    # The event must carry the in-flight stage name
    _p1_stage="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.stage // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_stage" ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage (stage=$_p1_stage)"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries in-flight stage" \
            "stage field empty in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi

    # The event must carry limit_s (the max_run_s value that was applied)
    _p1_limit="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="pipeline.end" and .data.status=="timed_out") | .data.limit_s // empty' \
        "$EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)"
    if [[ -n "$_p1_limit" && "$_p1_limit" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s=$_p1_limit"
    else
        assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P1: pipeline.end event carries limit_s" \
            "limit_s field absent or non-numeric in timed_out pipeline.end event"
    fi
fi

# ── P2: idle between dispatches — watchdog fires between stages ─────────────
print_test_section "P2: watchdog fires even when engine is idle between dispatches"

# Reset state/events for fresh run
rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"
mock_plugin_factory "fast-one" "agent" 0 >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "fast-two" "agent" 0 >/dev/null

# Stage 1: returns immediately; Stage 2: sleeps long
# max_run_s=2 — the run's total wall time must exceed 2s for the watchdog to fire.
# Stage 2 is a slow blocker (sleeps 30s) so the watchdog fires while stage 2
# is still dispatched (demonstrating the watchdog runs independently of stage state).
# The "between dispatches" case is demonstrated by the fact that stage 1 completed
# successfully before the watchdog fired — the watchdog did not need a stage to be
# actively dispatching in order to arm and fire.
FAST_TWO_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/fast-two-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-one/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_one_run() {
    $(mock_v2_result_line fast-one)
    return 0
}
PLUG
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/fast-two/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
fast_two_run() {
    : > "${FAST_TWO_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_v2_result_line fast-two)
    return 0
}
PLUG

set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-two-stage --goal "run-timed-out test p2" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p2.stderr"
p2_rc=$?
set -e

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: runner exits non-zero" "1" "$p2_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p2_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline status=timed_out (watchdog fires regardless of dispatch state)" \
        "timed_out" "$_p2_status"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

# fast-one must have completed (stage 1 finished before watchdog fired)
_p2_fast_one="$(jq -r '.stage_statuses.fast_one // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ "$_p2_fast_one" == "complete" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: fast-one completed before watchdog fired (watchdog fires idle too)"
else
    # fast-one may not have completed if watchdog fired before it — still proves watchdog works
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P2: watchdog fired (stage may or may not have run before it)"
fi

# ── P3: TERM-ignore → KILL within TERM + 10s ────────────────────────────────
print_test_section "P3: stage that ignores SIGTERM is dead within TERM + 10s"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

# Stage that traps SIGTERM and does NOT exit, sleeps indefinitely
TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/term-ignore-pid"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/slow-stage/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
slow_stage_run() {
    : > "${SLOW_STAGE_STARTED}"
    # Record our PID so the test can check it is dead
    printf '%s\n' "\$\$" > "${TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE}"
    # Trap SIGTERM and ignore it (only SIGKILL can stop this)
    trap '' TERM
    sleep 120
    $(mock_v2_result_line slow-stage)
    return 0
}
PLUG

_p3_start="$(date +%s)"
set +e
# max_run_s=2 → watchdog fires at 2s, sends TERM; stage ignores it;
# watchdog escalates to KILL at 2+10=12s. The runner must exit within ~15s.
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 30 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-single --goal "run-timed-out test p3 term-ignore" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p3.stderr"
p3_rc=$?
set -e
_p3_elapsed=$(( $(date +%s) - _p3_start ))

# Runner must exit (not hang past 30s timeout)
assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits non-zero (not still running)" "1" "$p3_rc"

# Runner must exit within TERM + 10s + buffer = 2 + 10 + 5 = 17s
if [[ "$_p3_elapsed" -le 17 ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer (elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s)"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: runner exits within TERM+10s+buffer" \
        "elapsed ${_p3_elapsed}s > 17s"
fi

# If stage PID was written, check the process is dead
if [[ -f "$TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE" ]]; then
    _ignore_pid="$(cat "$TERM_IGNORED_PID_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ "$_ignore_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        if kill -0 "$_ignore_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
            assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: TERM-ignoring stage process is dead after TERM+10s" \
                "PID $_ignore_pid is still alive"
        else
            assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P3: TERM-ignoring stage process is dead (PID $_ignore_pid killed)"
        fi
    fi
fi

# ── P4: release stage runs on timed-out exit path ───────────────────────────
print_test_section "P4: always_run release stage executes on timed-out exit path"

rm -f "$STATE_FILE" "$EVENTS_JSONL"

mock_plugin_factory "outcome"  "agent" 0 "" ""         >/dev/null
mock_plugin_factory "teardown" "tool"  0 "" "teardown" >/dev/null

# Outcome (flow) stage: sleeps 30s (will be killed by watchdog)
OUTCOME_STARTED="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/outcome-started"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/agent/outcome/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
outcome_run() {
    : > "${OUTCOME_STARTED}"
    sleep 30
    $(mock_v2_result_line outcome)
    return 0
}
PLUG

# Release (teardown) stage: drops a marker to prove it ran
RELEASE_MARKER="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/release-ran-on-timeout"
cat > "$PLUGINS_ROOT/tool/teardown/plugin.sh" <<PLUG
teardown_run() {
    : > "${RELEASE_MARKER}"
    $(mock_v2_result_line teardown)
    return 0
}
PLUG

set +e
( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" \
    --template timeout-with-release --goal "run-timed-out test p4 release" ) \
    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p4.stdout" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p4.stderr"
p4_rc=$?
set -e

assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: runner exits non-zero on timed-out path" "1" "$p4_rc"

if [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]]; then
    _p4_status="$(jq -r '.status // empty' "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    assert_eq "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: pipeline status=timed_out" "timed_out" "$_p4_status"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: pipeline-state.json written" "state file not found"
fi

if [[ -e "$RELEASE_MARKER" ]]; then
    assert_pass "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: release (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path"
else
    assert_fail "[#1944/SPEC-1] P4: release (always_run) stage ran on timed-out exit path" \
        "release marker not found — always_run stage did not execute"
fi

print_test_results
exit $((FAIL > 0))

The integration test run-timed-out-test.sh looks well-formed - the syntax `( cd "$OVERLAY_REPO" && ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=2 timeout 25 bash "$RUNNER" ... )` is valid bash syntax (unlike the precedence test).

Now I need to understand the full state of things. Let me focus on what's actually failing and why.

1. **run-limit-precedence-test.sh** - Has a syntax error at line 173. The fix would be to change `ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S="not-a-number" \` followed by `( cd "$MISCFG_OVERLAY" && bash "$RUNNER" ... 

I'm now thinking about the second failing test, run-watchdog-clean-exit-test.sh, which timed out after 2 minutes - suggesting the runner itself hangs when executing the test fixtures. It starts with ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=30, so the watchdog should terminate it well before the 2-minute mark unless the watchdog mechanism itself isn't functioning correctly. I suspect the issue is that the watchdog subshell arms itself to send SIGTERM/SIGKILL to the process group, but this might not properly reach the runner if it's a child process nested differently than expected.

If that were true though, the test would die immediately rather than hanging for two minutes—but it dies at the 2-minute bash timeout, not the 30-second watchdog limit, meaning the runner is just hanging rather than being killed. Looking back at the watchdog's actual implementation, it traps TERM, sleeps for the limit, then arms an abort sentinel and sends TERM to the negative process group ID before presumably following up with KILL.

Tracing where `_RUNNER_RUN_PGID` gets set, it's captured via `ps` on the runner's own PID, falling back to `$$` if that fails—so the watchdog ultimately kills the entire process group that the runner itself belongs to.

But this raises a problem: if the test shell hasn't called `setsid` or `set -m`, it shares that same process group, meaning the watchdog would kill the test shell too, not just the runner. The test wraps its invocation in a subshell, but a plain `( ... )` subshell doesn't create a new process group on its own, so I need to check whether the PGID actually differs between the test and the runner.

If the watchdog did kill the test shell, the test would exit immediately rather than hang for two minutes, which suggests either the watchdog never fires or it fires but fails to kill due to some permission or PGID mismatch issue. I'm looking at the test code that wraps the runner invocation with `ZBUILD_MAX_RUN_S=30`, capturing stdout/stderr and the return code with `set +e`/`set -e` around it.

I suspect the hang stems from the runner failing to resolve the `extends: simple` reference in the watchdog-single template, or some other initialization stall rather than the watchdog logic itself.

Since the previous run timed out, I can't just retest directly—I need to reason through how template lookup works. The runner likely searches `.zbuild/templates/` first before falling back to the system's `config/templates/simple.yaml`, and if that resolution path is broken or slow, that would explain the stall with the clean-exit test.

The real question is whether `watchdog-single.yaml`'s stage definitions fully override `simple`'s stages or simply merge with them, since `simple` has many stages but the mock only sets up `intake`. If stages merge rather than replace, the runner would try to find plugins for stages the mock never provides, which could be causing the failure.

# resolve_template_file <id> <repo_root>
#
# Returns the path to the effective template file via stdout:
#   - If <repo_root>/.zbuild/templates/<id>.yaml exists: validate extends:,
#     merge stages: and stage_definitions: over the base (ADR-016 full-replace),
#     write to a temp file, and print that path.
#   - Otherwise: print config/templates/<id>.yaml (shipped path, no merge).
# Exits 1 with a structured error if extends: is missing or the base is absent.
resolve_template_file() {
    local id="$1"
    local repo_root="${2:-$_TEMPLATE_RESOLVER_ROOT}"

    local per_repo_file="$repo_root/.zbuild/templates/${id}.yaml"
    local shipped_file="$_TEMPLATE_RESOLVER_ROOT/config/templates/${id}.yaml"

    if [[ ! -f "$per_repo_file" ]]; then
        echo "$shipped_file"
        return 0
    fi

    local extends_id
    extends_id="$(awk '/^extends:[[:space:]]/ { v=$0; sub(/^extends:[[:space:]]+/, "", v); sub(/[[:space:]]*$/, "", v); if (v != "" && v != "null") { print v; exit } }' "$per_repo_file")"

    if [[ -z "$extends_id" ]]; then
        echo "template-resolver: per-repo template '${id}' is missing required 'extends:' key" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local base_file="$_TEMPLATE_RESOLVER_ROOT/config/templates/${extends_id}.yaml"
    if [[ ! -f "$base_file" ]]; then
        echo "template-resolver: per-repo template '${id}' extends '${extends_id}' but config/templates/${extends_id}.yaml does not exist" >&2
        return 1
    fi

    # Write merged file to temp dir (TEST_TEMP_DIR in tests, mktemp in production).
    local merged_file
    if [[ -n "${TEST_TEMP_DIR:-}" ]]; then
        merged_file="${TEST_TEMP_DIR}/zbuild-tpl-${id}-$$.yaml"
    else
        # macOS/BSD mktemp requires XXXXXX at end (no trailing extension).
        # Mirrors the ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/name.XXXXXX pattern used elsewhere.
        merged_file="$(mktemp "$(zbuild_engine_tmpdir)/zbuild-tpl.XXXXXX")"
    fi

    # ADR-016 lock 1 is "full replace: there is no field-level merge with the
    # shipped file." A NEW-shape override (ADR-027: top-level `flow:` plus
    # per-stage sections) already IS the whole template, so full replace means
    # using it verbatim.
    #
    # Without this branch the awk below — which knows only the OLD shape's
    # `stages:`/`stage_definitions:` blocks — copies the base wholesale and
    # appends nothing, because a new-shape override has neither block. The
    # override is discarded, the BASE template runs, and nothing says so. The
    # implementation contradicted the ADR for every new-shape override; the spec
    # wins (CLAUDE.md).
    #
    # `extends:` stays required and its base still has to exist (locks 2 and 3):
    # those are about declaring lineage, not about merging fields.
    if awk 'BEGIN{rc=1} /^flow:[[:space:]]*$/ {rc=0; exit} /^flow:[[:space:]]*\[/ {rc=0; exit} END{exit rc}' "$per_repo_file"; then
        cp "$per_repo_file" "$merged_file"

So the mechanism becomes clear: the runner's PGID equals the subshell PID (S), and when the watchdog sends TERM to process group -S, it kills the runner and subshell but leaves the test shell untouched since it belongs to a different group (T, its own PID).

Tracing through the test: the subshell forks from the test shell, then execs `bash $RUNNER` inside it, so the subshell's own PID becomes the runner's PGID. When the runner queries its own PGID with `ps -o pgid= -p $$`, it gets back that subshell PID, and the watchdog's kill targets that exact process group -- which doesn't include the test shell, so the test shell survives. The mock plugin writes an intake result JSON and returns immediately, so that's not the hang. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# core/pipeline/runner.sh — Pipeline orchestrator (issue #83, #208, #222, #225)
# ADR-001 (plugin contract), ADR-006 (resume contract), ADR-009 (platform-aware modularity),
# ADR-011 (pluggable orch backend)
set -euo pipefail

_RUNNER_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
_ZBUILD_ROOT="$(cd "$_RUNNER_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=../contract/version.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/contract/version.sh"

source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/vision.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/vision.sh"
# ADR-025 (Wave 15-B #684) abort-propagation helpers — sourced before any
# dispatch site can call them; idempotent source guard inside.
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/abort-propagation.sh"
# #796 / ADR-021 v3 R1: pipeline final status helper honoring on_max=continue.
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/runner-final-status.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/runner-final-status.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-open-items.sh"   # run_end_words, open_items_markdown (#2330)
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/output/stage-colors.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/state/atomic.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/state/resume.sh"
# shellcheck source=../state/issue-lock.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/state/issue-lock.sh"
# shellcheck source=../state/run-cap.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/state/run-cap.sh"
# shellcheck source=../state/layout.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/state/layout.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/identity.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/identity.sh"
# #887: capture whether the operator PINNED any events location BEFORE
# event-bus.sh defaults them to $HOME/.zbuild/state — so per-run isolation
# overrides only the default, never an explicit operator/test override.
_ZBUILD_EVENTS_PINNED=""
[[ -n "${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR:-}${ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL:-}${ZBUILD_EVENTS_DB:-}" ]] && _ZBUILD_EVENTS_PINNED=1
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/plugin-registry/registry.sh"
# shellcheck source=../config/config.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/config/config.sh"
zbuild_config_init
# shellcheck source=../memory/contract.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/memory/contract.sh"
memory_init || { echo "runner: memory backend failed to initialize" >&2; exit 1; }
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/detect/platforms.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/template.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/template-resolver.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/resolver.sh"
# #2105: warm the manifest and discovery caches HERE, in the runner's own file
# scope, before contract.sh's source-time _orch_load_backend walks the tree
# through `< <(discover_plugins)` — a walk whose memo dies in that process
# substitution, 2.5s before main() gets to its own prewarm (#1614 / #2090).
# Filled once at this scope, every subshell below inherits it.
if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    yaml_cache_prewarm "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}"
fi
if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    discover_plugins "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi
# shellcheck source=../orch/contract.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/orch/contract.sh"
# Strategy modules (ADR-009 §fanout/sequential/composite, issue #222; map ADR-047)
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/fanout.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/sequential.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/composite.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/strategies/map.sh"
# Runner helpers extracted from this file in #279 to keep it under the
# CLAUDE.md 500-line cap.
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/dispatch.sh"
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/state_helpers.sh"
# ADR-020 (#496) pre-flight inter-stage data contract validator.
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/contract-validator.sh"
# #507 verdict-driven stage-complete indicator (ADR-019 / ADR-020 amendment).
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/verdict.sh"
# ADR-055 §1 / ADR-054 §2 (#1826): the runtime half of the input contract —
# declared inputs become resolved paths and are handed to `run`. Every behaviour
# it adds is unconditional as of #1825; sourced unconditionally
# because _runner_validate_startup_preflight delegates its renderer here.
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/input-resolve.sh"
# #2152 (ADR-065 §3): fill the input-resolve maps HERE, in this shell. Every
# reader runs `_inputs_stage_manifest` inside a `$( )`; without this fill each
# of the ~40 reads per run rescanned every manifest (2,255 awks on a mocked run).
if declare -F _inputs_scan_manifests >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _inputs_scan_manifests "${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/plugins}" 2>/dev/null || true
fi
# #1823 (ADR-054 §4): rc ∈ {0,1} — the narrowing, the observation captured before
# it, and the one place a legacy engine rc becomes a word.
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/dispatch-rc.sh"
# #1823: the throttle marker the router arms and this dispatch boundary reads.
# Sourced for the marker helpers, not the classifier — the router's own detector
# runs inside the plugin subshell and cannot hand its finding back any other way.
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/router-rc-classify.sh"
# ADR-021 (#512) outer-cycle orchestrator (F1, flag-gated by ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED).
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh"
# ADR-039 (#1131) parallel stage-group executor (sibling of the cycle orchestrator).
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/pipeline/parallel-orchestrator.sh"
# ADR-050 (#1581) prior-work reuse: generic, stage-agnostic artifact persistence
# to the state branch (zbuild/state/issue-<N>). The runner restores prior artifacts
# once at startup and snapshots at each stage boundary; it names no stage.
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"
# ADR-052 (#1640): the per-run worktree is engine-owned run infrastructure, so
# the runner — not any plugin — acquires it before the first stage dispatches.
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/worktree.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/worktree.sh"
# #2264: a stage can leave HEAD off the run branch; every stage end puts it back.
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-branch.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-branch.sh"
# ADR-054 §11 (#1944): run-level wall-clock limit resolver lives in stage-limits.sh
# alongside all other limit-resolution functions.
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/stage-limits.sh"

_usage() {
    # Usage shown on error or --help. Unix convention: stderr (#619).
    cat >&2 <<EOF
Usage: runner.sh --issue <N>|--goal "<text>" [--dry-run] [--template <id>]
                 [--resume] [--from-stage <stage>] [--no-resume] [--force]
  --issue <N>       GitHub issue number to work
  --goal "<text>"   Pipeline goal description (alternative to --issue)
  --dry-run         Print the stage plan without executing anything
  --template <id>   Pipeline template to use (default: simple)
  --resume          Resume an existing run (skip completed stages)
  --from-stage <s>  Skip ahead to stage <s> when resuming (emits warning)
  --no-resume       Recreate: start fresh even if a state exists and restore no
                    prior-run work (default: resume, reusing prior work;
                    ZBUILD_RESUME=0 is the same, #2225)
  --force           Resume even if status=aborted
  --self-host       Dogfood zBuild's own engine: redirect read-only contract-
                    grammar libs to a working-tree snapshot (#963, ADR-023)

Environment:
  ZBUILD_PLATFORM_OVERRIDE  Force a single platform; detection short-circuits.
  ZBUILD_SCOPE_PATHS        Newline-delimited scope paths; written as '+ <path>' entries.
  ZBUILD_SELF_HOST          Set to 1 to enable self-host mode (same as --self-host).
  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR   Override dir contract-reader stages source grammar libs from.
EOF
}

# Helpers extracted to dispatch.sh / state_helpers.sh in #279:
#   _find_plugin_for_stage       → core/pipeline/dispatch.sh
#   write_scope_override
#   _update_stage_status         } → core/pipeline/state_helpers.sh
#   _set_pipeline_status
#   (+ their _zbuild_runner_set_* jq filter helpers)

# Globals (not local) so EXIT trap can read them after main() returns.
_runner_run_id="" _runner_issue="" _runner_ended=false _runner_state_file=""
# ADR-054 §11 (#1944): run-level watchdog globals — PID of the watchdog background
# subshell (killed by the EXIT trap on clean exit) and the resolved limit in seconds.
_RUNNER_WATCHDOG_PID=""
_RUNNER_MAX_RUN_S=""
# #1878: last reported snapshot-failure reason, so a static precondition is
# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.
_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON=""

# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
_runner_retry_budget() {
    local v=""
    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
    (( v > 5 )) && v=5
    printf '%s' "$v"
}

# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
    _runner_ended=true
    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
    case "$v" in
        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
        *) return 1 ;;
    esac
    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
    _runner_ended=true
    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
    local latest="" n=0 d k
    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
    done
    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
        return
    fi
    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
_runner_note_push_failure() {
    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
}

# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. Only when HEAD carries
# commits past the intake baseline. Advisory: a failure is reported, never fatal.
_runner_push_work_branch() {
    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    local _base=""
    [[ -f "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" ]] && _base="$(cat "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_base" ]]; then
        local _ahead; _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
    fi
    local _err
    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
        return 0
    fi
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
    local _sd="${1:-}" _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch=""
    [[ -f "$_sd/intake-branch.txt" ]] && read -r _branch 2>/dev/null < "$_sd/intake-branch.txt"
    _branch="${_branch//[[:space:]]/}"
    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
        reattached)
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
        diverged)
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
    esac
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
# never blocks a run.
#
# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
# item 1 of #1807.
#
# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
# and leaving no trace anywhere.
_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
    # push had nothing to send.
    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0

    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
        saved)
            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
            ;;
        failed)
            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
            # no channel to surface on.
            #
            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
            fi
            ;;
        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
        *) : ;;
    esac
    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
    local _leak=""
    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
        # code commits still go to the work branch.
        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
    fi
    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
    return 0
}

# ─── stage-start time cache (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()

# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).
_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS=""

# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
_runner_now_ms() {
    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$ovr"
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
        return 0
    fi
    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
}

# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
_runner_status_comment_reap() {
    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        local i
        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
            sleep 0.1
        done
        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
_runner_now_short() {
    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
        return 0
    fi
    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
    local out
    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
    printf '%s' "$out"
}

# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
_runner_duration_token() {
    local stage="$1"
    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '?s'
        return 0
    fi
    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
        printf '?s'
        return 0
    fi
    local ms=$(( now - start ))
    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
    else
        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
    fi
}

# ─── _runner_export_scope_allowlist <state_dir> (ADR-043) ────────────────────
# Redaction by construction: the per-run scope allowlist, exported as
# ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST so route_to_model can redact without a plugin passing
# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).
_runner_export_scope_allowlist() {
    local state_dir="$1"
    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the
    # engine no longer reads plan.json by path.
    if [[ -s "$rec" ]]; then
        csv="$(jq -r '(.scope_files // []) | unique | join(",")' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
    fi
    # #1874: the shape floor is part of the scope — computed here, mechanically,
    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds
    # the files a shape change owes. Memoised per scope: this runs every stage.
